experience.fullDescription:
Completed My Internship as a Software Development Intern (Supply Chain & GIS)

Over the past month, I had the opportunity to work on a live enterprise application and gain hands-on exposure to how large-scale software systems are built, maintained, and improved in real-world environments.

This internship helped me move beyond simply writing code and understand how technology supports business operations, workflow management, traceability, location-based systems, and data-driven decision-making.

Some of the areas I worked with and learned about:

🔹 Frontend development and user experience design
🔹 Backend APIs and system integrations
🔹 Database management and data handling
🔹 GIS and geospatial data workflows
🔹 Supply chain processes and operational workflows
🔹 Inventory movement concepts such as inbound and outbound operations
🔹 Warehouse and logistics management systems
🔹 User roles, permissions, and access management
🔹 Git version control and branching strategies
🔹 Debugging issues across frontend, backend, and database layers
🔹 Understanding servers, deployments, and production environments

One perspective that changed significantly during this internship was my understanding of AI. Throughout college, I often heard discussions about AI replacing jobs and reducing opportunities for developers. However, working in a real-world development environment showed me a completely different side of it. I saw how AI is being used to improve productivity, speed up development, assist in debugging, simplify research, and help teams solve problems more efficiently. Rather than replacing people, AI has become a powerful tool that enables professionals to focus on higher-value work and deliver better results.

One of the most valuable lessons from this experience was understanding how different modules of an application work together—from user onboarding and operational workflows to inventory tracking, reporting, warehouse operations, and system administration. Seeing how a live product functions behind the scenes gave me a much deeper appreciation for the complexity and collaboration involved in building reliable software.

Working on a live project also taught me the importance of writing maintainable code, collaborating with a team, investigating issues methodically, and ensuring that every change works reliably within a larger system.

I'm grateful to my mentors and teammates for their guidance and support throughout this journey. This experience has strengthened both my technical and problem-solving skills, broadened my understanding of how technology supports real-world business operations, and motivated me to continue learning and growing as a software developer.
